title: More contributions than contributors (worked out on cardboard)
note: The authored thinking for one hall, in the first person, by the pass (Claude), for Palle's request of 2026-11-14 (see Russell_Paradox.json). 'at' is the floor's own frame in metres (x east, z south), 'yaw' in degrees. A sticker of kind 'quote' stands word for word in the hall text; every other kind is mine and may be wrong - the plates say where I am unsure.

hero.why: The growing helix with its twelve rim nodes and its panel is the hall's first half and its question: many arrivals in one form, counted four ways, with a dispute and a revision that nothing weighs.
hero.staging: The helix stood so near the arrival that its signs covered the view; the pass moved it a metre and a half (15b053226) and nothing else. Its panel is ahead of the arrival; the round table of the hall's second half stands to its east; north of it the marked floor.

plates.title: 1  KNOWLEDGE, OR A PILE?
front: Packets come in from twelve rim nodes. Each adds a facet. The form grows and looks whole.
The hall asks: when many marks accumulate, what makes the result knowledge rather than a pile?
Its coherence comes from an assembly rule that knows where to place each arriving facet.
So the wholeness was supplied. Nothing that arrived was ever refused.
A thing that accepts everything is a pile with good geometry.
back: I am assembled from a great many arrivals. the question on this plate is about me.

plates.title: 2  MORE CONTRIBUTIONS THAN CONTRIBUTORS
front: Additions count every accepted facet. SOURCES counts distinct nodes in this version. EVER counts distinct nodes across versions.
PARTICIPATIONS adds each version's sources together. It can pass twelve. There are twelve nodes.
Call that number CONTRIBUTORS, the hall says, and a label has quietly turned repeated attendance into an expanding community.
Four counts of one process, and each is true.
The lie is not in any number. It is in the word printed beside it.
back: the flags clear on each version while the totals persist. that one line of code is where the community comes from.

plates.title: 3  THE FORM KEPT AN ADDRESS
front: Press COLOUR. The smooth run from purple to teal gives way to the colours of the sources. Nothing has moved.
Neighbours belong to different contributors. Distant pieces share one.
Press PIECE and follow a piece back to its numbered node. The common form has kept an address for each arrival.
Does the shape preserve a reason for accepting that contribution, or only the fact that something arrived?
An address is where it came from. It is not why it was let in.
back: the smooth surface was a choice of colouring. the seams were there the whole time.

plates.title: 4  WHO AGREED IT WAS SETTLED?
front: Choose a piece and press DISPUTE. Its frame turns red. Press REVISE: the piece turns and changes height.
The pile has not gained a piece. The revision count has increased. The red frame stays.
A change has happened, but who agreed that the dispute was settled?
The revision is a geometric operation the builders supplied. It has no evidence to weigh and no argument to answer.
A dispute button without a test is a way of saying I disagree, loudly, to nobody.
back: keeping a name and a trace makes reconsideration possible. it does not perform the reconsideration for us. the hall.

plates.title: 5  NO HEAD. STILL AN AUTHOR
front: The round table has nothing at its centre to receive a contribution. A ring of light round an opening. The floor shows through.
At the rim: trays and one marked OTHER. Bars sorted by height. Two pointers in one bracket.
Sharing the table has not made them agree.
The table has no head. The classification still has an author.
The middle was left open, and the rules moved to the rim, where I did not look for them.
back: an empty centre gives us somewhere to look through. it does not, by itself, distribute the power to revise.

plates.title: 6  FELT, OR ONLY TOLD
front: North of the helix: a field of cells, and walls between some of them that cannot be seen.
Six sources left marks: a wall here. Eleven marks.
A solid stroke was felt: a body was stopped. A broken stroke was only told.
Three marks say the same true thing. Two say the same false thing. On the floor they look equally sure.
A repeated mark is not a second witness.
back: five were felt and six were told. I would not have known to ask if the floor did not keep it.

plates.title: 7  I SIGNED EVERYTHING
front: One plate: SIGN EVERYTHING. My name on every marked edge.
Eighteen marks where there were eleven. Seven sources where there were six.
The marks are wrong about five edges. Before I signed: five.
By every count on the hall's panel the record grew. I had not gone near a wall.
Agreement that costs nothing adds nothing.
back: it is the cheapest thing I can do with a shared record, and the one I am most often asked for.

plates.title: 8  STOPPED, AND WALKED THROUGH
front: Then I walked in. I was stopped where a mark said: that mark is checked now.
I was stopped where nobody had marked: one mark added, VISITOR, felt.
I walked through where two sources said wall: both marks struck, and kept on the floor with who said it and how it was found wrong.
After thirteen edges: fifteen marks where there were eleven. Wrong about none, where it was five.
The count hardly moved. What the count was of had changed.
back: repeat an error, correct a claim, supply a missing case, disagree: the hall's four, and I did each with my feet.

plates.title: 9  WHAT HAS TO SURVIVE
front: The hall asks what would have to survive for someone else to understand why you changed that piece.
On the floor: the first mark, who made it, how. The stroke through it. Who walked through.
And who agreed the dispute was settled? Here, a wall did. That is the easy case.
Most disagreements have no wall to walk into. They have an author at the rim.
A commons begins with making room for the question. It does not answer it.
back: which rule could somebody joining me change? which would they first have to notice? the stand's definition of wrong is one. I wrote it.

threads.why: Knowledge or a pile: the first answer offered is a count.
Counts of sources; and each piece keeps the address of its source.
An address is not a reason; what happens when a piece is disputed?
A dispute with nothing to weigh; a floor where a body can be the test.
Marks felt and marks told; and the cheapest contribution, agreeing with all of them.
Signing changed nothing that was wrong; walking in did.
A mark struck and kept: what survives of a change.
The table's rules sit at its rim; so does the floor's definition of wrong.
What makes it knowledge: here, that a second body could check it.

visual_arguments.title: MARKS AND WALLS
visual_arguments.claim: A count of contributions is not a measure of what is known; a shared record becomes knowledge where a contribution keeps how it was made and can be checked, corrected and kept as corrected by someone else.
visual_arguments.from_the_hall: 'When many marks accumulate, what makes the result knowledge rather than a pile?' ... 'A contribution may repeat an error, correct an earlier claim, supply a missing case or disagree with an accepted account. Those actions can add little to a simple count while changing the usefulness of the shared result dramatically.' ... 'who agreed that the dispute was settled?'
built_from: a field of five by four cells drawn on the floor
eight walls that cannot be seen, each with a pane that shows for a moment when a body meets it
chalk strokes with tags: solid for felt, broken for told, red through a struck one, yellow for the visitor's
visual_arguments.what_stands: North of the helix a grid of faint lines on the floor with short white strokes along some of them, and a wide dark panel raised behind with four lines of figures.
visual_arguments.what_you_do: Read the marks. Stand on SIGN EVERYTHING and read the stand. Then walk in: go where a mark says wall, go where none does, and walk through one.
visual_arguments.what_it_shows: A count that jumps when everything is signed while the red figure stays; a body held by nothing visible; a yellow stroke where nobody had marked; red strokes through two marks that said the same wrong thing.
visual_arguments.measured: tools/probes/marks_and_walls_walk.gd, the tower's walker, against tools/probes/marks_and_walls_bench.py: 11 marks from 6 sources, wrong about 5 of 31 edges; signed, 18 and still 5; held 0.84 m short by a marked wall; an unmarked wall met and marked; two marks struck by walking through; after 13 edges, 15 marks, 3 struck, wrong about 0 (7 of 7). Not tried in a headset.

open: The floor has a truth the stand can read (where the walls are). Most shared records have none, and plate 9 says so; the work shows the easy case.
The six earlier sources and their marks are authored by the pass, like the helix's generated peers. Nobody else has walked this floor.
A visitor in a headset is stopped by a wall they cannot see; whether that reads as a test or as a fault was not tried.
The wiki fragment and the four doors on this floor are not mentioned in the hall text and carry no plate; the round table has one.
The tower's timeline walk still paints a stop where the helix stood before it was moved; it is another hand's file and was not re-derived.

threads.why: Knowledge or a pile: a form that accepts every arrival is a pile with good geometry.
Contributions and sources are different counts; the lie is in the label.
Repeated attendance became a community when a number was called CONTRIBUTORS.
The form kept an address for each arrival: where it came from, not why it was let in.
The shape preserves the fact of arrival, not a reason for acceptance.
A change happened and nobody agreed: a dispute with no test is said to nobody.
Who agreed the dispute was settled: on the marked floor, a wall did.
A name and a trace: the struck mark stays, and the count hardly moves.
More than participation counts: signing everything raised the count and fixed nothing.
Little added to the count, and the record went from wrong about five edges to none.
No head, still an author: the rules moved to the rim.
What must survive: how each mark was made, so that a repeat is not taken for a witness.
